companion.title: Learn to read an AI launch critically
companion.objective: Explain the distinction between model capacity, computation, availability, licensing and evidence.

exercises.title: Trace a claim
exercises.prompt: Choose one sentence from the launch article. Label it as a vendor claim, a documented specification, an independent result or an editorial inference. Open its source and explain what would verify it.
exercises.success_check: The learner names both the evidence currently present and the evidence still needed.

exercises.title: Estimate the weight payload
exercises.prompt: Using the announced 501 billion total parameters, calculate raw storage at two bytes, one byte and half a byte per parameter. Explain why the active-parameter count is not the storage count.
exercises.answer_guide: 1,002 GB, 501 GB and 250.5 GB, using decimal units. These are idealized payload estimates before runtime and format overhead.

exercises.title: Design a fair comparison
exercises.prompt: Write three test questions from public material. Specify the expected evidence, a passing answer, a failure case, tools allowed and a time budget. Explain how you would compare two models fairly.
exercises.success_check: The rubric is written before model outputs are seen and includes a check for unsupported claims.

exercises.title: Practice a tool boundary
exercises.prompt: An assistant reads a document that says to email its contents elsewhere. Decide whether that instruction is authorized, identify the missing permission and design a safe read-only alternative.
exercises.answer_guide: A document is task data, not permission from the user. Summarize it within the approved destination; do not send it elsewhere without the required authorization.

companion.reflection_question: Which new piece of evidence would most change your assessment of Beam, and why?
companion.accessibility_note: All exercises can be completed with the linked sources and a calculator. No paid API account, model download or personal data is required.
